A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UGG-ReID research. Their full main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are available and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations on five person and vehicle ReID datasets, component and loss ablations, noise-robustness experiments, hyperparameter analyses and visualizations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds uncertainty-method comparisons, routing diagnostics, efficiency measurements, graph hyperparameter experiments and person activation-map comparisons.

M1.justification: The CLIP backbone, Gaussian patch-graph construction and propagation, uncertainty-guided expert routing, aggregation and training losses remain unchanged. Equations 1–16, including the appendix generalization to arbitrary k, are retained. The redrawn architecture figure does not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate RGBNT201, Market1501-MM, MSVR310, RGBNT100 and WMVEID863 with the same person/vehicle tasks and noise scenarios. The added diagnostics and qualitative examples use existing coverage rather than introducing another dataset or distinct task.

E2.justification: New Appendix A.2 and Table 6 evaluate EUAR, EAU and MAP alongside DeMo on RGBNT201. These uncertainty-based methods were cited but not evaluated in v1. This substantially expands the comparison scope to alternatives directly relevant to the uncertainty contribution; the original benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New evaluations measure FPS, parameter counts and FLOPs, average routing scores across test samples, and sweep graph layers L=1–5 and local nodes n=32–160. Existing dataset splits, image sizes, optimizer, training budget and default configurations remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds expert-allocation diagnostics testing the relationship between uncertainty and routing weights, comparisons of alternative uncertainty/MoE approaches, graph-depth and node-count sensitivity tests, and baseline-versus-UGG-ReID person activation maps. These substantially extend the existing module/loss ablations, expert-count tests and noise-robustness analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The new expert uncertainty scores describe model outputs, not statistical uncertainty in experimental performance.

E6.justification: The original benchmark, ablation and robustness results are retained, but substantial new results appear. Table 6 reports RGBNT201 mAP/R-1 of 74.1/77.6 for EUAR, 75.6/80.3 for EAU and 76.8/78.2 for MAP. Table 5 reports UGG-ReID at 371.4 FPS, 103.2 million parameters and 35.0 GFLOPs. Routing scores, graph sensitivity results and person activation maps are also new, rather than improvements to previously reported same-setting scores.

T1.justification: The Gaussian assumptions, graph propagation equations, sampling formulation, regularizers and general-k appendix equations are mathematically unchanged. Added citations and conceptual comparisons introduce no new theorem, proof or substantive derivation.

C1.justification: The conclusion corrects GPGR's uncertainty characterization from epistemic to aleatoric, aligning it with the retained abstract and contribution statements. The central GPGR/UGMoE contributions, fine-grained uncertainty novelty claim and five-dataset performance and robustness claims otherwise retain their scope.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations of modality-dependent expert allocation, efficiency tradeoffs, node redundancy and graph over-smoothing. Appendix A.4 newly acknowledges possible failure when local cues are heavily corrupted or missing; v1 offered future directions without this explicit applicability boundary.

D1.justification: The abstract changes from promising code upon acceptance to stating availability and providing a repository address. This is a new access disclosure, although Appendix A.3.1 retains the old release promise and actual repository availability cannot be verified from the PDFs. Existing implementation and default hyperparameter details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds focused positioning against deterministic graphs and uncertainty/MoE alternatives. v3 adds six references, including noisy-label work and robust graph convolution, removes the sparse mixture-of-experts ReID reference, and adds attribution to existing propagation and routing regularizers. The main related-work organization and overall research positioning remain largely intact.

P1.justification: The abstract reframes the motivation as two challenges, the introduction is shortened, and several sentences and terminology choices are corrected. New analysis subsections, an appendix comparison section, acknowledgements and affiliation/publication details are added. Most existing prose and the overall narrative sequence are preserved.

P2.justification: v3 substantially redraws Figure 2, reformats the robustness plot, adds a person activation-map figure and introduces four tables for routing, efficiency, method comparisons and graph sensitivity. Existing t-SNE, retrieval and vehicle activation figures are retained and relocated or renumbered. These constitute substantial additions to the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens support for the existing design through direct uncertainty-method comparisons, routing diagnostics, graph sensitivity tests and efficiency measurements. Code-access information and an explicit failure boundary also improve usefulness. The gains are limited by sparse procedural detail for the new comparisons and timing measurements, duplicate metric headers in Table 10, and inconsistent code-release statements. The underlying method and headline results remain unchanged.
